chapters.html:
It happened quietly, as things like this often did. One moment, Mydei was chaperoning Phainon after their spar, where the latter had insisted—almost demanded—they find somewhere to relax. “A drink will do us good,” Phainon had said, his grin sharp and teasing as he patted Mydei on the shoulder. “You can brood into your pomegranate juice, and I can actually enjoy myself.”

Mydei hadn’t argued. He rarely did when Phainon was like this, all energy and light, with that mischievous glint in his eyes that suggested he wouldn’t take no for an answer. Instead, Mydei had followed, allowing himself to be led through the city streets and up to a rooftop bar Phainon had decided was “quiet enough” for the both of them.

It was a modest place, tucked high above the bustle of Okhema’s streets, with tables spaced far enough apart to give the illusion of privacy. The sunlight cast everything in a warm, golden glow, the perpetual brightness of the city filtering down like a quiet hum. Mydei found a corner table, one that overlooked the city, and settled into his chair, letting the familiar weight of his pomegranate juice rest in his hand.

Phainon, of course, was anything but still. He leaned back in his seat, legs stretched out, his drink—a syrupy concoction too sweet for Mydei’s tastes —perched in one hand. “See? Isn’t this nice?” he said, grinning as he tilted his glass toward Mydei. “You should try enjoying yourself for once. It won’t kill you.”

“Debatable,” Mydei replied, his tone dry, though his lips twitched faintly at the corners.

The exchange was brief, comfortable, and Mydei found himself settling into the rhythm of it, his gaze drifting to the cityscape. For a while, there was peace—a rare moment of quiet where he could simply exist, the weight of the day not quite pressing so heavily on his shoulders.

The next, there was some local standing before Phainon, their hands trembling as they poured their heart out.

Phainon, of course, was oblivious to the weight of Mydei’s glare, his golden eyes fixed entirely on the flustered speaker. Mydei’s fingers curled tighter around his glass, tension rippling through his arm as he resisted the urge to stand, to loom, to make his presence unmistakable.

Before that, this is what transpired and how it got to this point; It was supposed to be a quiet evening. But then, of course, nothing was ever truly quiet where Phainon was concerned.

At a table not far from theirs, a small group of locals had gathered, their laughter bright and easy as they passed their drinks between them. Mydei had barely spared them a glance at first—another group of strangers, indistinct from the rest.

But then, his attention shifted as he noticed one of them—a young man, nervous and fidgeting with the edge of his sleeve. The others in the group seemed to take note of his hesitation, their voices dropping to murmurs, their expressions turning sly and encouraging.

“You’ve been staring at him all night,” one of them whispered, grinning as they nudged the nervous man.

“Now’s your chance,” another added. “What’s the worst that could happen?”

The young man’s face flushed, and he shook his head quickly, mumbling something about how it was a bad idea. But the others persisted, their voices light but insistent. “You’ve got nothing to lose,” one of them said, leaning closer. “Just go for it!”

And then, reluctantly, the man rose to his feet, his steps hesitant as he made his way toward Phainon.

Mydei noticed him immediately. The nervous shuffle of his feet, the way his hands twisted at his sides, the faint flush of color on his cheeks. It was the kind of awkwardness that would have been endearing to someone like Phainon—someone who thrived on connection, on human vulnerability. But to Mydei, it was something else entirely.

He tensed, his fingers tightening around his glass as the man approached their table.

Phainon, for his part, seemed pleasantly oblivious. He was in the telling a joke, his golden eyes bright with mischief, when the man cleared his throat.

“Excuse me,” the man said, his voice shaking slightly.

Phainon turned toward him, his smile unbroken, his attention shifting easily as though this were the most natural interruption in the world. “Oh? What can I do for you?”

The man hesitated, his gaze flickering nervously between Phainon and the ground. “I—I just… I wanted to say something. If that’s alright.”

Phainon’s head tilted slightly, his expression patient and encouraging. “Of course,” he said warmly. “Go ahead.”

The confession came out in a rush—words tumbling over themselves in their eagerness to be heard. The man spoke of admiration, of watching Phainon from afar, of how he’d been captivated by his charm and presence. It was clumsy and unpolished, but there was a sincerity in it that even Mydei couldn’t deny.

Not that it mattered.

Because what truly mattered was the audacity of it all.

They knew. Everyone knew. The relationship between him and Phainon wasn’t some well-guarded secret, whispered only in shadowed corners. It was known, a fact of the city as undeniable as the light that never faded.

And yet, here this man was, pouring his heart out in full view of Mydei, as if he didn’t exist. As if his presence at Phainon’s side was merely a coincidence, an afterthought.

Jealousy burned hot and fast in his chest, sharp and consuming. His grip on the glass tightened, his knuckles whitening as the tension surged through him. His jaw clenched, his breath steady but shallow as he forced himself to remain still, his eyes locked on the scene unfolding before him.

Phainon, as always, handled it with grace.

“I’m flattered,” he began, his voice soft and kind, carrying just enough weight to show he meant it. “Truly, I am. It takes a lot of courage to say something like that, and I admire you for it.” He paused, his smile warm but tinged with regret. “But I’m afraid I can’t return your feelings. My heart already belongs to someone else.”

The man blinked, his face a deep red, but managed a quick, awkward nod. “I—I understand,” he stammered. “Thank you for hearing me out.”

Phainon’s smile widened slightly, his tone lightening as he added, “And thank you for sharing. That’s no small thing.”

The man offered a quick bow of his head before retreating, his steps hurried as he returned to his table.

Mydei’s eyes followed him, his expression impassive but his presence sharp, like a blade held just out of sight. The man’s friends greeted him with hushed words, their faces a mix of amusement and pity. One of them placed a comforting hand on his shoulder, whispering something that made him nod slightly, though his expression remained sheepish.

But then, Mydei caught it—another whisper, this one lower but no less deliberate.

“It’s not your fault,” one of the friends said, their gaze darting briefly toward Mydei before turning back to the man. “He’s not who he used to be. Mydei’s tainted him. Phainon deserves better—someone like you.”

The words hit like a spark to dry tinder, and the tension in Mydei’s chest erupted into something sharper, something darker. His grip on his glass tightened, the cool surface pressing harder against his palm, but he didn’t move. He didn’t need to.

Instead, he shifted slightly in his seat, his posture as calm as ever, but the subtle change in his presence was undeniable. His gaze, sharp and unyielding, swept across the group with a weight that seemed to press the air between them.

The friend who had whispered stilled under his stare, their smile faltering as they glanced away, their confidence wavering beneath the force of his silent intimidation.

Phainon, who had been watching the whole time, broke the tension with a laugh.

“You’re scaring them again,” he said lightly, his golden eyes gleaming with amusement as he turned to Mydei. “Honestly, you’re going to give someone a complex one of these days.”

Mydei didn’t respond, his gaze shifting back to his drink as though nothing had happened.

Phainon’s laughter softened, and he leaned forward, his voice low but warm. “You don’t need to do that, you know.”

“Do what?” Mydei asked evenly, though the edge in his tone betrayed him.

Phainon’s smile grew, and for a moment, he looked as though he might say more. But then he simply shook his head, leaning back with an easy grin. “Never mind.”

he moment passed, but the weight of it lingered, pressing down on Mydei like a shadow that refused to fade. The silence between him and Phainon stretched, comfortable for Phainon, but far from it for Mydei. He could feel the tension in his chest, coiling tighter with every passing second, every lingering whisper. It was as if the world had shifted slightly, and now he was on the outside, trapped in the spaces between what he wanted and what was happening.

He hadn’t realized just how much it had been eating at him—the jealousy, the simmering possessiveness, the quiet fear that Phainon might look at someone else the way he had looked at him all this time. Not that Phainon had ever given him reason to doubt him—not really. There was no betrayal in Phainon’s eyes, no hidden agenda beneath that easy smile, that warmth. And yet, here he was, faced with the undeniable truth that people— strangers, at that—were still capable of reaching out to Phainon, of seeing him the way Mydei had always seen him.

The thought gnawed at him. Why wasn’t Phainon more affected? Why hadn’t he hesitated, even for a second, before rejecting the confession? It wasn’t as if it were the first time someone had tried to make their feelings known to Phainon—he had always been the center of attention, the object of affection and admiration. But this time, something felt different. This time, the words had come in full view of Mydei, and there was something in their tone, something in the desperate sincerity, that made it sting more than it ever had before.

Does he feel that way about me? Does he feel like… he belongs to me, the way I belong to him?

The thought slipped through his mind like a whisper, but he shoved it away, focusing instead on the way his fingers curled around his glass. His grip was tight, almost painful, but he didn’t loosen it. He didn’t want to.

“I’m fine,” he muttered to himself, barely audible over the gentle hum of the bar. The words were hollow, and he knew it. They didn’t convince him, but they were all he could offer in the face of the storm that raged inside him.

He glanced at Phainon then, sitting just across from him, unaware of the turmoil churning in Mydei’s chest. Phainon had returned to his easygoing self, sipping his drink and laughing at something one of the nearby patrons had said. His golden eyes sparkled with a warmth that could light up the entire city, and for a moment, Mydei simply watched him.

The jealousy twisted again, sharp and unforgiving, as he studied Phainon’s smile—the same smile that had once been reserved just for him. He could feel it deep in his gut, this quiet, aching need to possess that smile, to make sure it was only ever his.

But then the whispers came back. They had already begun to echo in his mind, the words of the local’s friend ringing loud and clear: Phainon deserves better—someone like you.

That part of the conversation had been an unwelcome intrusion into his thoughts, and yet it had stuck with him, like a splinter buried under the skin, a constant reminder of his own inadequacies. He had never been the best for Phainon, had never been the one to bring out his most carefree side the way others did. Wasn’t that what Phainon deserved? Someone who could give him more—who could be more than Mydei could ever be?

Was he holding Phainon back?

The thought stung like a raw wound, too familiar and too real to ignore. He had always known he wasn’t like other people. He wasn’t the one to lead the conversations, to be the center of attention. He had always been the watcher, the observer, content to stand in the background while Phainon reveled in the spotlight. But was that enough for someone like him?

Mydei’s gaze flickered back to Phainon, who was now engaged in conversation with the bartender, a light laugh slipping past his lips. The easy, effortless grace with which Phainon navigated the world—it was something Mydei both admired and envied. Was that something he, someone so deeply bound by duty, could ever offer Phainon? Did he deserve to be the one Phainon always turned to?

His thoughts spiraled further, but he caught himself.

No.

The realization was sharp, cutting through the noise of his mind. He knew his worth—had always known it. He wasn’t some shadow lurking at the edges of Phainon’s world. He wasn’t the one who would fade when someone else came along. He had earned his place at Phainon’s side— earned his position in his heart.

But that didn’t stop the jealousy from coiling tighter, didn’t stop the possessive instinct from flaring up, this gnawing fear that Phainon might one day realize there was someone else, someone who could give him everything Mydei couldn’t.

Someone who isn’t so… tied down.

The thought flickered through his mind, and just like that, the self-doubt threatened to take root again. Was that what it was? Was it that Phainon was too free, too unbound by anything, anyone—too unclaimed—for someone like Mydei, who had too many ties to his past, to his city, to his responsibilities?

Mydei’s hand shifted, the tight grip on his glass almost painful as he crushed the idea before it could take hold. No.

He wasn’t going to entertain this.

Phainon was his. And he would not let anyone—not even himself—ruin that. He would not let anyone tell him what Phainon deserved. He was enough.

But the words of the friend lingered, like a faint taste of bitterness. Mydei’s gaze snapped back to Phainon as the man laughed again, the sound like music that wrapped around him, soothing something deep in his chest. Mydei’s heart beat faster, and for a moment, he let the jealousy slide into something sharper—something possessive. He didn’t care if it was wrong. He didn’t care if Phainon deserved better. He was the one here. He was the one Phainon had chosen.

And that, in itself, was all that mattered.

laughter around them faded, the words spoken in hushed tones growing quieter as Mydei sat back, his fingers still gripping his glass, the weight of it a comforting, steady pressure against his palm. The jealousy had dulled to a quiet burn in his chest, but the discomfort had not dissipated. His thoughts still spun, tangled up in doubt and insecurity, and yet, he had forced himself to maintain the stillness. To sit there, as if nothing at all had bothered him.

But Phainon, ever perceptive, noticed.

The laughter in the air had softened, but Phainon’s eyes were on him now, and Mydei could feel the weight of that gaze, the way it lingered a second too long. The smile that had been so bright moments ago faded, his expression shifting to something gentler, something that held a quiet concern.

“Hey,” Phainon said, his voice softer now, his tone carrying a trace of hesitation. “Are you alright?”

The question, simple and without accusation, settled in the air between them like a weight, and Mydei felt his chest tighten. He didn’t answer right away, didn’t know how to respond. Not because he didn’t want to—no, it wasn’t that. He just wasn’t sure how to give voice to the quiet storm swirling inside him.

Phainon waited, still watching him with that concerned frown pulling at the edges of his lips. Mydei’s breath hitched slightly, but he quickly regained his composure. His gaze shifted, unable to meet Phainon’s for a moment.

“I’m fine,” Mydei said, his voice even, though there was a coldness to it that he couldn’t quite mask.

Phainon didn’t seem convinced. The silence between them stretched out, long and uncomfortably heavy. His golden eyes searched Mydei’s face, a flicker of frustration crossing his expression before he exhaled softly. “Mydei…” he started again, but the words were cut off as Mydei stood abruptly, the action so sudden it seemed to startle Phainon.

“I have to go,” Mydei said, the words blunt, final.

Phainon blinked, caught off guard by the sudden shift. He stared up at Mydei for a long moment, his face a mixture of surprise and something else —something that Mydei couldn’t name. But before he could say anything, Mydei was already moving, already heading for the exit, not sparing another glance in Phainon’s direction.

The sound of coins hitting the table—sharp and deliberate—made Mydei pause for a fraction of a second, but he didn’t look back.

Phainon, without a word, had slammed a hefty amount of money onto the table, more than enough to cover their drinks. His movements were swift, almost frantic as he quickly pushed his chair back and stood, ready to follow. Mydei, however, didn’t slow down. The weight of his footsteps was the only sound in the air, the sharp contrast of their hurried pace filling the space between them.

Phainon caught up easily, his long strides closing the gap in an instant. “Mydei,” he called out, his voice low, hesitant. “Wait.”

But Mydei didn’t. He walked faster, his frustration simmering beneath the calm surface, a tight knot of irritation curling in his chest.

“Mydei,” Phainon said again, his voice firmer now, and before Mydei could ignore him completely, Phainon’s hand closed around his wrist, pulling him to a stop.

The touch was gentle but insistent, and for a moment, Mydei felt a flicker of surprise at the force of it. He didn’t look at Phainon, but he felt the heat of his gaze. “What’s going on?” Phainon asked, the concern in his voice now unmistakable, his eyes searching Mydei’s face.

Mydei stood still for a moment, his jaw clenched. He could feel the sharp pressure of Phainon’s grip on his wrist, warm and familiar, but it only made the heat in his chest grow more intense. The jealousy, the possessiveness, the concern for something he couldn’t explain—it all boiled to the surface.

“I said I’m fine,” Mydei finally replied, his voice strained, barely keeping the edge of frustration from breaking through.

Phainon didn’t let go. His fingers tightened just a fraction, his touch grounding, unyielding. “Don’t lie to me,” he said quietly, his voice laced with a tenderness that almost cut through Mydei’s wall of calm. “Something’s wrong. Please. Talk to me.”

The words struck deeper than Phainon realized, but Mydei wasn’t ready to face them yet. He pulled his wrist from Phainon’s grasp, not harshly, but with enough force to make the point. “I need some air,” he said shortly, his voice rougher than he’d intended.

He started walking again, his movements quicker now, almost agitated. The sound of Phainon’s footsteps behind him was steady, but it only made the knot in Mydei’s stomach grow tighter. He needed space. He needed to be away from Phainon, from everything.

But just as he reached the edge of the street, ready to turn the corner, Phainon’s hand was on his wrist again, this time more firmly, more desperate. He wasn’t letting Mydei slip away this time.

“Stop running away,” Phainon said, his voice barely above a whisper.

“I’m not running away,” he muttered, the words flat but heavy.

Phainon’s grip softened, but it didn’t let go. He stepped closer, his voice soft and steady as he spoke. “Tell me what’s wrong, Mydei.”

For a moment, Mydei hesitated, but suddenly, as if possessed, he grabbed Phainon by the shoulder and practically dragged him to a secluded alleyway.

Phainon looked at the other surprised, “Mydei—?”

The alleyway was empty, the dim light of Okhema’s eternal twilight casting long shadows between the buildings. Mydei’s grip on Phainon’s wrist was firm, almost urgent, as he pulled him away from the noise and the crowd, his mind still swirling with jealousy, frustration, and a quiet possessiveness he couldn’t bury. He could feel the weight of Phainon’s gaze on him, the curiosity, the confusion, but Mydei didn’t care. Not right now.

The need to claim Phainon, to make sure that no one could ever threaten what they had, was too strong. Mydei could feel the heat rising within him, the frustration, the raw desire for something more than just unspoken words. He needed Phainon to understand—to feel it.

When they reached the alleyway, Mydei didn’t give Phainon the chance to speak, didn’t give him time to ask questions. Instead, he yanked him toward the wall, the force of it making Phainon stumble slightly before Mydei’s body was pressed against his. For a moment, all that existed was the tension between them, the heat of their bodies and the raw edge of Mydei’s emotions.

Phainon’s breath hitched in surprise, but he didn’t push away. His eyes searched Mydei’s face, a flicker of something—concern, confusion— crossing his features. “Mydei—” he began, but Mydei was done with words.

His mouth found Phainon’s in a fierce kiss, urgent and deep. His hands moved to the back of Phainon’s neck, pulling him closer, his body pushing harder against Phainon’s as if he were trying to merge them into one. Phainon gasped against his lips, but Mydei didn’t give him a chance to respond. The kiss was raw, desperate, as if every word that had gone unspoken was being poured into the frantic press of their mouths.

Mydei’s heart pounded in his chest, his body alive with the need to prove something—to show Phainon what he was feeling, to claim him in a way he hadn’t been able to before. His hands moved to grip Phainon’s shirt, tugging him closer, his fingers almost trembling with the intensity of it. The kiss grew deeper, more desperate, as if the walls Mydei had built around his emotions were finally crumbling, piece by piece.

When he finally pulled away, his breath coming in ragged gasps, his eyes were dark, full of something fierce and possessive. He could feel Phainon’s chest rising and falling against his, their hearts beating in tandem, but the words that followed were a raw confession Mydei had been holding back for too long.

“I won’t share you,” Mydei breathed, his voice thick with emotion, his hands sliding down Phainon’s chest as he leaned in, his lips brushing against Phainon’s ear. “I don’t want to share you. Not now. Not ever.”

Phainon’s breath caught in his throat, and for a moment, Mydei saw that flicker of surprise in his eyes. But it was quickly replaced by something else —something deeper, more understanding. Phainon didn’t pull away. Instead, he responded, his hand sliding to Mydei’s waist, his fingers tightening around him as he kissed him again, this time with a gentler urgency, a quiet promise in the way their mouths met.

Mydei’s heart pounded, the heat of the kiss fueling the fire inside him. He kissed Phainon harder, his fingers now gripping Phainon’s shirt, the need to feel him, to have him, taking over. The world outside the alleyway didn’t matter anymore. Nothing mattered except the feeling of Phainon’s body against his, the way their hearts seemed to sync with each kiss.

“I’m not going anywhere,” Phainon murmured between kisses, his voice low, reassuring, and full of the same intensity. “I’m here, Mydei. Only with you.”

The words, the weight of them, settled deep in Mydei’s chest. It was all he needed to hear. The possessiveness in his veins began to shift, morphing into something softer, something grounded in the quiet trust they shared. He wasn’t holding Phainon down. He wasn’t losing him. Phainon had always been his, and Mydei would keep it that way.

Phainon’s hands slid up to Mydei’s hair, tugging him back into the kiss, this time slower, deeper, the urgency of before tempered by something that felt like an unspoken understanding between them. Mydei let out a breath, his fingers now working at the buttons of Phainon’s shirt, the tension between them growing with each passing second.

But for now, it was enough. Just the two of them, tangled in the alleyway, as if nothing else existed. Phainon was his, and Mydei was finally, truly okay with it.

Mydei’s hands moved with deliberate purpose, dragging Phainon closer, forcing the space between them to shrink until they were tangled together in the dim light. The kiss they shared was slower now, but the intensity hadn’t waned—if anything, it had deepened, becoming a silent language that only they understood.

Mydei pulled away again, his breath ragged as he moved to the side of Phainon’s neck, pressing a searing kiss to the sensitive skin there. Phainon’s hands gripped his shoulders, but before he could react further, Mydei’s teeth found the soft flesh of his neck, grazing the skin with a sharp, possessive bite.

Phainon let out a soft gasp, his body shuddering slightly at the sensation, and Mydei’s lips followed, leaving a trail of marks in their wake. Mydei bit down again, harder this time, drawing a low moan from Phainon as he marked him, over and over, the sensation of his lips on Phainon’s skin growing more insistent, almost frantic.

Phainon’s breath hitched, his hands trembling slightly on Mydei’s shoulders as he finally spoke, his voice laced with a quiet, amused realization. “You’re jealous,” he murmured, his tone soft but knowing.

Mydei froze for just a moment, the bite he had been about to leave faltering before he let go of Phainon’s neck. He didn’t pull away completely but instead rested his forehead against Phainon’s, his grip tightening around him. He had been so wrapped up in the need to mark him, to show him what he couldn’t say out loud, that he hadn’t even realized how obvious he had been.

“I wasn’t… I’m not,” Mydei started, his voice a little too defensive, but Phainon only smiled softly, running a hand through his hair in a soothing gesture.

“You don’t have to hide it,” Phainon teased lightly, his tone a playful contrast to the heat still simmering between them. “I get it. It’s okay, Mydei. I’m not going anywhere.”

Mydei’s jaw clenched, but something inside him softened at the tenderness in Phainon’s voice. He hadn’t meant to let his jealousy show so easily, but he couldn’t deny that the intensity of his feelings for Phainon had pushed him beyond the point of containment.

“I just…” Mydei began, but Phainon silenced him with a gentle smile, his hands cupping Mydei’s face now, pulling him in close.

“You’re allowed to feel that way,” Phainon said softly, his voice laced with affection. “You don’t have to be so guarded with me, you know.”

Mydei exhaled slowly, his shoulders sagging slightly, but he didn’t break eye contact with Phainon. “I don’t want to lose you,” he admitted, the words coming more easily now than he expected.

Phainon’s smile softened into something more intimate, more knowing. “You won’t,” he promised, his hands sliding down Mydei’s chest, the warmth of his touch grounding Mydei in the moment. He leaned in closer, his voice lowering. “I’m not going anywhere. You’re my only one.”

Mydei’s breath caught at the conviction in Phainon’s tone, but before he could speak, Phainon pulled back slightly, his eyes narrowing with a sudden realization. “Wait…” he said, studying Mydei with a mix of curiosity and amusement. “Is this about the guy back there?”

Mydei’s expression hardened, a wave of frustration sweeping over him. “What?” he muttered, trying to mask his emotions, but Phainon’s perceptive gaze cut through him like a blade.

Phainon leaned in again, his grin teasing, but there was no mistaking the softness in his voice. “You’re jealous, aren’t you?”

Phainon continued, “Listen to me, Mydei. You’re mine. And I’m yours. There’s no one else, and there won’t be,” Phainon murmured, his hand gently cupping Mydei’s cheek, guiding his face back toward him. “You don’t have to fight for that. It’s never been about competition. It’s always been us.”

The weight of those words hit Mydei harder than he expected, and for a moment, all he could do was stare, his emotions conflicting—relief, frustration, a deep, burning possessiveness that he didn’t know how to put into words.

Phainon, seemingly satisfied that Mydei understood, couldn’t resist the urge to tease him. “It’s cute, you know,” he murmured, his grin widening, eyes twinkling mischievously. “Seeing you like this, all worked up. But,” he leaned closer again, his breath warm against Mydei’s ear, “I think I like it even more when you’re a little less guarded.”

Mydei’s jaw tightened, irritation bubbling up again as he opened his mouth to respond, but before he could get the words out, Phainon moved with unexpected speed. One arm slid behind Mydei’s neck, pulling him in close as Phainon rested his head against him, his other arm trailing down Mydei’s waist, his touch light but deliberate.

“Mydei,” Phainon whispered softly, his voice dripping with playful heat, “Let’s continue this somewhere else.”

The words, delivered with that certain quiet authority, shot a spark of desire through Mydei’s veins. The intimacy in Phainon’s touch, the way his body pressed so close, sent a jolt of warmth through Mydei’s chest, grounding him in the moment and yet pushing him toward the edge of something he couldn’t quite control.

He looked at Phainon, his face a mixture of annoyance and something more intense, something deeper. “You’re really going to keep doing this, huh?”

Phainon’s eyes glinted with mischief, but there was still that soft assurance in his expression. “Oh, I absolutely am,” he teased, his voice low and playful. “You’ll get used to it. But for now… why don’t we take this somewhere a little more private?”

Mydei’s breath caught again as Phainon leaned in once more, his lips brushing against Mydei’s ear, sending a shiver down his spine. The tension, now thick and heavy, had shifted. Mydei couldn’t escape it, nor did he want to.

“Are you sure?” Phainon murmured, his tone almost playful, but there was an undeniable edge to it, as if he knew exactly how to push Mydei’s buttons. “Because once we’re there, I’m not letting you go.”

Mydei swallowed hard, every fiber of his being screaming to let go, but still, he couldn’t. “Lead the way,” he said, his voice barely above a whisper.

Phainon smiled—satisfied, confident—and without another word, he guided Mydei away, his fingers trailing down Mydei’s side. Only Mnestia knows how many beds they broke after that.
